hook.en: Names, words, passwords, sentences: most programs handle text. In Java a String is an object, with a toolbox of methods for searching, cutting and comparing text.

objectives.en: Create strings and explain their immutability
Write programs that process a string character by character

narration.en: Names, words, passwords, sentences: most programs handle text. In Java a String is an object, with a toolbox of methods for searching, cutting and comparing text.

body.en: A String is an object of the class java.lang.String holding a sequence of characters. String s = "Java"; creates it. Strings are immutable: methods such as toUpperCase() return a new String and leave the original unchanged. Characters are indexed from 0 to s.length() − 1 (length is a method for strings). To compare contents use s.equals(t) or s.equalsIgnoreCase(t); == only compares whether two references point to the same object.

body.en: Most string programs loop over the characters: for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { char ch = s.charAt(i); … }. The Character class tests and converts: Character.isLetter, isDigit, isWhitespace, isUpperCase, toUpperCase. Typical tasks: count vowels, reverse a word, check a palindrome, count words (spaces + 1 after trimming), change the case of each letter, or build a new string with +. StringBuffer (and StringBuilder) is a mutable alternative with append, insert, reverse and setCharAt.
